2608.26887.title: Planting a Latent Variable in Natural-Looking Text: a More Realistic Test of Belief States in LLMs and Their Link to Concept Geometry
2608.26887.paper_summary: LLMs are thought to track "belief states," i.e., running probability distributions over the latent variables that govern language (Shai et al., 2024; Sarfati et al., 2026), but so far this has only been comprehensively demonstrated on toy synthetic data and in a few isolated case studies. It has also never been empirically connected to the geometry of LLM features (the concepts interpretability finds in model activations). In this work, we plant a controllable latent variable inside natural-looking text. An LLM teacher writes ordinary text while we "subliminally" steer it along one of K = 8 unrelated sparse autoencoder directions at each token, with the active directions following a ring-shaped Markov chain. A small transformer model trained on this corpus does indeed track the Bayesian posterior belief about our planted latent variable. Moreover, it also arranges the 8 states themselves on a ring, in the exact order of the Markov chain, which is supporting evidence that a concept's geometry can be formed by the statistical dynamics of the latent variable behind it.
2608.26887.paper_summary_zh: LLMs 被認為追蹤「信念狀態」，即對支配語言的潛在變數運行概率分佈（Shai et al., 2024; Sarfati et al., 2026），但到目前為止，這僅在玩具合成數據和幾個孤立的案例研究中得到了全面的證明。它也從未在實證上與 LLM 特徵的幾何形狀聯繫起來（概念可解釋性在模型激活中找到的內容）。在這項工作中，我們在自然看起來的文本中植入了一個可控的潛在變數。一位 LLM 教師在我們「潛意識地」引導它沿著 K = 8 個無關的稀疏自編碼器方向的每個標記時，寫下普通文本，這些活躍的方向遵循一個環狀的馬爾可夫鏈。訓練於此語料庫的小型Transformer模型確實追蹤了我們植入的潛在變數的貝葉斯後驗信念。此外，它還將這 8 個狀態本身按照馬爾可夫鏈的確切順序排列在一個環上，這支持了概念的幾何形狀可以由其背後潛在變數的統計動態形成的證據。
2608.26887.author: Alexandru-Iulius Jerpelea et.al.
